desc: An operation that produces the same result no matter how many times it is executed. Critical for safe retries.
Mechanism to signal the producer to slow down when the consumer cannot keep up, preventing resource exhaustion.
When many waiting processes are woken simultaneously by a single event, causing resource contention.
Design pattern that detects failures and prevents cascading failures by failing fast instead of waiting for timeouts.
Distributed hashing scheme that minimizes key remapping when nodes are added or removed from a hash table.
A distributed system can only provide two of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance.
Space-efficient probabilistic data structure for set membership testing. Can have false positives but never false negatives.
Distributed algorithm coordinating all processes in a distributed atomic transaction on whether to commit or abort.
Modifications written to a log before being applied, ensuring durability and atomicity after a crash.
Resource is shared until a process attempts to modify it, at which point a private copy is created.
Hash table scheme using two hash functions where insertion may evict existing entries to their alternate position.
Family of protocols for achieving consensus in a network of unreliable processors.
Disproportionate amount of load concentrating on a single resource, causing bottlenecks.
Minimum number of votes needed to approve an operation. Typically majority (N/2+1) in Raft/Paxos.
Keeps multiple versions of data so readers see a consistent snapshot without blocking writers.
Consensus algorithm designed for understandability. Uses leader election, log replication, and safety guarantees.
Peer-to-peer communication protocol inspired by how epidemics spread. Used in Cassandra, Consul.
Process where distributed nodes designate a single node as the organizer to coordinate tasks.
Algorithm for generating partial ordering of events and detecting causality violations in distributed systems.
Conflict-free Replicated Data Type. Data structure that can be replicated across multiple computers with strong eventual consistency.
Splitting a large database into smaller, faster, more manageable parts called shards distributed across multiple servers.
Time delay between a write on the primary database and its propagation to replica databases.
Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. Four properties guaranteeing database transaction validity.
Basically Available, Soft state, Eventually consistent. Alternative to ACID for distributed NoSQL systems.
Sequence of local transactions where each updates data and publishes an event. Used for distributed long-running transactions.
Consistency model guaranteeing that if no new updates are made, eventually all reads will return the last updated value.
Strongest consistency guarantee. Every operation appears to execute atomically at a single point in time.
Transaction isolation level where concurrent transactions produce the same result as if executed serially.
Situation where two or more processes are each waiting for the other to release a resource.
Processes continuously change state in response to each other without making progress.
A process is perpetually denied necessary resources to proceed with its work.
Behavior where the output depends on the sequence or timing of uncontrollable events.
Variable used to control access to a common resource by multiple processes in a concurrent system.
Mutual exclusion object. Used to prevent multiple threads from simultaneously accessing a shared resource.
Lock where a thread repeatedly checks until the lock becomes available, avoiding expensive context switches.
Compare-and-Swap. Atomic instruction used for implementing lock-free data structures and synchronization primitives.
False-positive in CAS where a value changes from A to B and back to A, making CAS incorrectly succeed.
Read-Copy-Update. Synchronization mechanism allowing reads to occur concurrently with updates.
Non-Uniform Memory Access. Memory access time depends on the memory location relative to the processor.
Smallest unit of data transfer between cache and main memory. Typically 64 bytes on modern CPUs.
Performance degradation when threads on different cores modify variables on the same cache line.
Instruction that enforces ordering constraints on memory operations performed by the CPU.
Translation Lookaside Buffer. Hardware cache for virtual-to-physical address translations.
Exception raised when a program accesses a memory page that is not currently mapped to physical memory.
Copy-on-Write. Fork uses this to avoid copying entire parent process memory until the child writes.
Linux kernel feature limiting, accounting, and isolating resource usage of process groups.
Data structure in Unix filesystems describing a file, storing its attributes and disk block locations.
Technique where data is transferred directly between kernel and application buffers without intermediate copies.
Monitoring multiple file descriptors to see if I/O is possible on any of them. select/poll/epoll/kqueue.
Linux scalable I/O event notification mechanism. O(1) operation regardless of the number of watched descriptors.
System call mapping files or devices into memory, enabling direct memory access to file contents.
Just-In-Time compilation. Converts bytecode to native machine code at runtime for performance.
Ahead-of-Time compilation. Compiles source code to native machine code before execution.
Garbage Collection. Automatic memory management that reclaims memory occupied by objects no longer in use.
Virtual method table. Mechanism used to support dynamic dispatch in object-oriented languages.
Resource Acquisition Is Initialization. Idiom where resource management is tied to object lifetime.
C++ feature that transfers resources from one object to another without copying, improving performance.
Algebraic Data Type. Composite types formed by combining other types, like sum types and product types.
Higher-Kinded Types. Type constructors that take other type constructors as parameters.
Communicating Sequential Processes. Formal language for describing patterns of interaction in concurrent systems.
Concurrency model where actors are universal primitives that communicate via message passing.
User-space threads scheduled by the runtime rather than the OS kernel. Used in Go (goroutines), Java (virtual threads).
Function that can suspend its execution and resume later, enabling cooperative multitasking.
Self-balancing tree data structure maintaining sorted data, optimized for disk reads. Foundation of most databases.
Log-Structured Merge-Tree. Data structure optimized for write-heavy workloads. Used in RocksDB, LevelDB, Cassandra.
Probabilistic data structure allowing O(log n) search complexity. Used in Redis sorted sets.
Prefix tree for efficient retrieval of keys in a dataset of strings. Used for autocomplete and IP routing.
Hash tree where each leaf node contains a data hash and each non-leaf node contains hashes of its children.
Probabilistic data structure for estimating the cardinality of a set with very low memory usage.
Probabilistic data structure for estimating the frequency of events in a data stream.
Fixed-size buffer that wraps around. Used for lock-free queues in high-performance systems like LMAX Disruptor.
Compressed bitmap data structure. Efficient for sparse integer sets. Used in Lucene, Spark, Druid.
Condition where a cluster splits into multiple partitions, each believing it is the active cluster.
Monotonically increasing number issued with a lease. Prevents zombie processes from corrupting data.
Technique where if a node is down, another node stores updates and delivers them when the node recovers.
Technique where stale data detected during a read is updated in the background to maintain consistency.
Background process that compares replicas and reconciles differences to maintain eventual consistency.
Quorum that allows writes to non-preferred nodes when the preferred nodes are unavailable.
Pattern where an operation is only executed if the object is in an appropriate state.
Pattern where a method call is suspended until a precondition is satisfied.
Lock allowing concurrent reads but exclusive writes. Optimizes read-heavy workloads.
Data structure or algorithm that guarantees system-wide progress without using mutual exclusion.
Stronger than lock-free. Every operation completes in a bounded number of steps regardless of other threads.
Pattern separating read and write operations for a data store. Often paired with Event Sourcing.
Storing state as a sequence of events rather than current state. Enables audit trail and temporal queries.
Ports and Adapters pattern. Isolates domain logic from external concerns via interfaces.
Strategy for handling fast producers in reactive streams by controlling the rate of emission.
Incremental migration strategy where a new system gradually replaces the old one by intercepting calls.
Deploying a helper component alongside the primary application to provide supporting features.
Proxy that handles network communication on behalf of the primary application.
Rate limiting algorithm where tokens are added at a fixed rate and consumed per request.
Rate limiting algorithm processing requests at a fixed rate using a FIFO queue.
Algorithm increasing the wait time between retries exponentially to reduce contention.
Adding randomness to retry intervals to avoid thundering herd of simultaneous retries.
Cache eviction policy that removes the least recently used item first.
Cache eviction policy that removes the least frequently used item first.
Lightweight check to verify service health before sending real traffic. Often implemented as health endpoints.
Gradually rolling out changes to a small subset of users before making them available to everyone.
Running two identical environments, switching traffic from one to the other during deployments.
Toggle that enables or disables features at runtime without redeploying code.
Deploying code to production but hiding it from users until it's ready to be revealed.
